Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having an impact of
Important.
A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed
severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the
References section.", "title": "Topic"}, {"category": "general", "text": "Each Red Hat AMQ Client enables sending, and receiving messages to or from AMQ Broker 7.

This update provides various bug fixes and enhancements in addition to the
client package versions previously released on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9
and 10.

Security Fix(es):

* protonj2: Apache Qpid ProtonJ2: Denial of Service via unbounded type nesting [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-67590)
* proton-j: Apache Qpid Proton-J: Denial of Service via unbounded symbol value caching [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-66257)
* proton-j: Apache Qpid Proton-J: Denial of Service due to excessive allocation [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-66273)
* proton-j: Apache Qpid Proton-J: Denial of Service via unbounded type nesting [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-66274)
* protonj2: Apache Qpid ProtonJ2: Denial of Service via unbounded symbol value caching [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-67588)
* protonj2: Apache Qpid ProtonJ2: Denial of Service via excessive memory allocation [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-67589)
* jackson-core: jackson-core: Denial of Service via incomplete fix in async JSON parser [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-68494)
* jackson-databind: Jackson-databind: Security bypass allows arbitrary code execution [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-54513)
* jackson-databind: jackson-databind: Arbitrary code execution via PolymorphicTypeValidator bypass [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-54512)
* artemis-core-client: Apache ActiveMQ: Denial of Service via crafted WireFormatInfo frame [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-50734)
* kerb-server: Apache Kerby: Kerberos pre-authentication bypass via unrecognized PA-DATA [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-57915)
* micrometer-core: Micrometer: Denial of Service via specially crafted gRPC requests [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-40983)
* micrometer-core: Micrometer: Denial of Service via specially crafted HTTP requests [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-40984)
* netty-handler: Netty: Denial of Service due to eager buffer allocation in TLS handshake [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-45416)
* netty-handler: Netty: Improper trust manager handling leads to hostname verification bypass [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-50010)
* netty-handler: netty-handler: IPv6 subnet rule bypass due to incorrect masking operation [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-44249)
* assertj-core: AssertJ: Information disclosure and denial of service via XML External Entity (XXE) [amq-cl-2025.Q2] (CVE-2026-24400)
* netty-codec: Netty: Denial of Service via excessive memory allocation in LZ4FrameDecoder [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-42583)
* netty-codec-http: Netty: Denial of Service via unbounded memory allocation in HTTP content decompression [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-42587)
* netty-handler-proxy: Netty: HTTP Header Injection via HttpProxyHandler Disabled Validation [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-42578)
* netty-codec-http: Netty: HTTP Request Smuggling due to improper handling of conflicting HTTP/1.0 headers [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-42581)
* netty-codec-http: Netty: Incorrect HTTP response parsing leads to data confusion [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-42584)
* spring-boot: Spring Boot: Weak pseudo-random number generation can lead to information disclosure. [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-40975)
* netty-codec-http: Netty: Request smuggling via incorrect parsing of HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer encoding extension values [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-33870)
* spring-boot: Spring Boot: Authentication bypass via misconfigured Health Group additional path [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-22731)
* qpid-proton-dotnet: Apache Qpid Proton-Dotnet: Denial of Service via unbounded symbol value caching [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-67465)
* qpid-proton-dotnet: Apache Qpid Proton Dotnet: Denial of Service via excessive memory allocation [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-67551)
* qpid-proton-dotnet: Apache Qpid Proton-Dotnet: Denial of Service via unbounded type nesting [amq-cl-2026.Q1] (CVE-2026-67552)

Bug Fixes and Improvements:

* ENTMQCL-4576 [qpid-jms] The combination of NMS DotNet AMQP producer and qpid-jms consumer doesn't handle the type of JMSReplyTo correctly.
* ENTMQCL-4574 [qpid-jms] Update kerb-simplekdc test dep to 2.1.2
* ENTMQCL-4573 [qpid-jms] Update ActiveMQ version in compatibility tests to 5.19.9
* ENTMQCL-4572 [qpid-jms] Update JUnit to version 5.14.4
* ENTMQCL-4571 [qpid-jms] Update commons io to version 2.22.0
* ENTMQCL-4570 [qpid-jms] Update mockito to v5.23.0
* ENTMQCL-4569 [qpid-jms] Update slf4j to version 2.0.18
* ENTMQCL-4568 [qpid-jms] Update jacoco plugin to 0.8.15
* ENTMQCL-4567 [qpid-jms] Update to Netty 4.1.137.Final
* ENTMQCL-4566 [qpid-jms] JMSConsumer receiveBody should throw if message is a bare Message instance
* ENTMQCL-4564 [protonj2] Update junit to v5.14.4
* ENTMQCL-4563 [protonj2] Update netty to latest release 4.1.137.Final
* ENTMQCL-4562 [protonj2] Update proton-j test dependency to v0.35.0
* ENTMQCL-4561 [protonj2] ROUND_ROBIN policy implementation error
* ENTMQCL-4560 [protonj2] Inconsistent has result returned from Binary type
* ENTMQCL-4365 [protonj2] Unit tests fails on io_uring detection

mitigations: Applications utilizing Netty's HttpProxyHandler must ensure that any user-controlled input used to populate outbound headers is rigorously sanitized to prevent CRLF injection. If comprehensive input sanitization cannot be implemented, restricting network access to the application that uses the HttpProxyHandler can reduce the attack surface.

Applications utilizing Spring Boot should avoid using the `${random.value}` property for generating cryptographic secrets or other security-sensitive data. Developers should review their application configurations and code to ensure that only cryptographically strong random number generators are used for such purposes. For UUID generation, `${random.uuid}` is not affected and can be used.

Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base or stability.

Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

To mitigate this issue, configure any reverse proxies or load balancers in front of Netty to either reject HTTP/1.0 requests containing both Transfer-Encoding: chunked and Content-Length headers, or to explicitly prioritize the Transfer-Encoding header over Content-Length for HTTP/1.0 traffic. This ensures consistent interpretation of message boundaries and prevents request smuggling attacks.

To mitigate this issue, configure applications utilizing Netty's `SslClientHelloHandler` to specify a non-zero value for the `maxClientHelloLength` parameter. This will enable the internal length validation, preventing the eager allocation of large memory buffers when processing crafted TLS ClientHello messages. Refer to your specific application's documentation for details on configuring Netty's TLS handler. A restart of the affected application or service is required for the configuration changes to take effect.

To mitigate this issue, restrict network access to services exposing Micrometer's gRPC endpoints to trusted clients only. Implement firewall rules to limit inbound connections to the specific ports used by gRPC. If gRPC functionality is not essential for the deployment, consider disabling it entirely to eliminate the attack vector. Any changes to network configurations or service settings may require a service restart to take effect, potentially impacting availability during the transition.

To mitigate this issue, restrict network access to services utilizing Apache Qpid Proton-J to trusted clients and networks only. Implement firewall rules to limit inbound connections to the specific ports used by these services. This operational control reduces the attack surface by preventing untrusted external access, but may impact legitimate client connectivity if not carefully configured.

To mitigate, ensure that application endpoints requiring authentication are not declared under paths already configured as Health Group additional paths within Spring Boot applications using Actuator. Review and adjust your application's configuration to prevent this overlap. A redeployment of the application is required for changes to take effect.

Upgrade com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-core to a fixed version, such as 2.18.8 or later, 2.21.4 or later, or the first fixed release in the applicable 2.22.x stream. For Jackson 3.x, upgrade to 3.1.4 or later, or the first fixed release in the applicable 3.2.x stream. If upgrading is not immediately possible, do not expose the non-blocking parser to untrusted, incrementally streamed JSON. Where feasible, use a synchronous parser or buffer and enforce strict request-size, connection-timeout, and concurrency limits at the ingress layer. Apply the upgrade as soon as possible because ingress limits reduce exposure but do not correct the parser defect.

Upgrade to version 2.18.8, 2.21.4, or 3.1.4 or later to address this vulnerability. If upgrading is not immediately possible, remove BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator.Builder.allowIfSubTypeIsArray() from the application’s ObjectMapper configuration to eliminate the affected deserialization path. Rebuild and restart the application to apply the configuration change.

As an additional mitigation, disable polymorphic deserialization of untrusted data where possible by avoiding or removing default typing features such as activateDefaultTyping() or enableDefaultTyping(). When polymorphic deserialization is required, restrict allowed subtypes using a strict whitelist of trusted application packages and avoid broad or permissive type validation rules.
